rationale: PINS the top-level-property attribution boundary, the defect the R7 endpoint probe MEASURED at 1,290 `Global` sources in clean files (998 calls / 147 references / 135 instantiates / 10 uses) on a 1,200-file every-Nth draw of bb_tests/repositories/kotlin@9b80c8ff. Three resolvers shared one declaration list that omitted `property_declaration`, so every edge in a top-level property's initializer or type clause fell through to `source_file` and was attributed to the literal `Global`. TWO halves are pinned, because the obvious over-correction (treat every property as a boundary) is a different defect: (1) a TOP-LEVEL property owns its initializer's call and its declared type — these are the pins that fail before the fix; (2) a MEMBER property's initializer and declared type belong to its CLASS, unchanged — the `parent.type === "source_file"` guard is the load-bearing condition and nothing else pins it. `buildModule` is not a stdlib leaf and `Holder` is not declared in this file, so both survive the stdlib and declared-type filters and the pins are about attribution only.

expectRelationships.note: TOP-LEVEL property owns the call in its own initializer. Before the fix this edge was `calls[Global->buildModule]`.
and the same property owns its own declared-type reference
`Paths.get(...)` is a QUALIFIED call, so the stdlib filter keyed on the bare leaf does not suppress it
a top-level property with no initializer still owns its declared type
MEMBER property: the class owns the initializer's call, NOT the property. The walk reaches class_declaration first, so the new branch is never reached here.

An EXTENSION property's accessor is a SIBLING of its declaration in the pinned wasm, so the walk crossed no declaration and this edge sourced to `Global` before the fix. The accessor belongs to the declaration written above it.
and the accessor's own declared type resolves through the same boundary
second member property, same rule — an edge is published for each, and both source to the class
a member property's declared type belongs to the class too

forbidRelationships.note: the fallback this fixture exists for. kotlin has no symbol named `Global`; R7 forbids a placeholder literal in a name-bearing field and every consumer downstream can match, count and display it.
